subject: FA.component and an individual measure of FA

messages.author: 38a666f7d265258c
messages.subject: FA.component and an individual measure of FA
parts:
Dear all,

 I am in the early stages of a project that aims to evaluate fluctuating asymmetry (FA) as a measure of developmental instability. To facilitate exploratory tests, I would like to have an individual measure of FA. I am hoping to use the FA.component that is returned from the bilat.symmetry function (obtaining an FA value by calculating the root-sum-of-squares the configurations), but was hoping to understand a little more clearly how FA.component coordinate configurations are calculated. 
 Do the FA.component coordinate configurations represent the individual's right-left differences minus the population's average right-left differences? I believe this is a method frequently advocated for isolating fluctuating asymmetry (found in, for example, Zelditch et al. 2012: 369 and Klingenberg and McIntyre 1998: 1375 - the latter being referenced for the bilat.symmetry function). I have looked at the function's code, but have to admit that I am relatively inexperienced in coding and so would appreciate guidance on the subject.
 Best regards,

   Ben W.

Klingenberg, C. P. and McIntyre, G. S. 1998. Geometric Morphometrics of Developmental Instability: Analyzing Patterns of Fluctuating Asymmetry with Procrustes Methods. Evolution 52 (5): 1363-1375.

Zelditch, M. L., Swiderski, D. L. and Sheets, H. D. 2012. Geometric Morphometrics for Biologists. A Primer. London: Academic Press.

parts:
Ben,

 

Please see the help file for bilat.symmetry, which states:

 

FA.component

The fluctuating asymmetry component for each specimen, found as the specimen-specific side deviation adjusted for the mean directional asymmetry in the dataset.

 

So yes, it does what you thought it does.

 

Dean

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Re: FA.component and an individual measure of FA
parts:
Ben,

 

As stated in the help file:

 

“The fluctuating asymmetry component for each specimen, found as the specimen-specific side deviation adjusted for the mean directional asymmetry in the dataset.”

 

When there are replicates for each individual, this is based on the individual’s mean values. The last few lines of code in the function calculates these:

 

X.ind.side <- model.matrix(~(side:ind) + 0, data = as.data.frame(dat.shape[-1]))

    ind.mns <- coef(.lm.fit(X.ind.side, Y))

FA.component <- ind.mns[-indsq, ] - ind.mns[indsq, ]

FA.component <- simplify2array(lapply(1:n.ind, function(j) {

        t(matrix(FA.component[j, ], k, p)) + mn.shape - mn.DA

    }))
